reference.title: Git History View
reference.shortdesc: The controls in the Git History view.

section.title: Overview
section.p: Open the view from the toolbar button, from Window Show View , or from a Show history action in a contextual Git submenu.

ul.li: The branch chooser filters the graph: all branches, all local branches, the current branch, or the current local branch.
(on by default) keeps the history in sync with the active editor.

The text filter can be used to narrow the list by message, date, author, commit ID, branch, or tag. When the field contains text, a clear (X) button appears. Clearing the filter keeps your current selection in view.

section.title: Status Labels
section.p: A status bar shows the current working copy, the branch, and the file whose history is displayed (when you are viewing the history of a single resource). These labels are interactive:

ul.li: Select the branch link to scroll the history table to the tip of that branch.
Select the X next to the file to clear the file filter and show the full repository history again. Turning off also clears the file filter.

section.title: History Table
section.p: Each row shows the graph, message, date, author, and commit ID, latest first. When the working copy has uncommitted changes, a grey node appears at the top of the graph, representing the future commit (it disappears once you commit or discard those changes).

Right-click a commit for actions such as , , , , , and . On the tip commit of the current branch, the contextual menu also includes (the pull action follows the type set in your preferences) and (these appear only when the branch has a tracked remote, and after a pull the view scrolls to the new tip).

Branch labels on a commit are interactive. Double-click a label to switch to that branch. Hover over a label to see its details. For a local branch, it shows the name, a current-branch marker, its tracking branch, and how far ahead or behind it is (counts of 100 or more show as 99+). For a remote branch, it shows the local branches that track it. The current local branch's label is highlighted. Right-click a label (rather than elsewhere on the row) for label-specific actions:

ul.li: (local branch) or (remote branch) - Selects the related branch's tip commit.
Delete... - Removes a local branch, after a confirmation.
- Opens the Branch Manager with the branch selected (local or remote).

section.title: Commit Details and Affected Resources
section.p: The pane shows the commit ID, parent, author, date, committer, any refs (branches and tags) on the commit, and the message. The committer date is shown next to the committer only when it differs from the author date (for example, after a rebase, cherry-pick, or amend). The pane lists the files the commit changed. Right-click a file to access these actions (which ones are available depends on how the file changed):

dlentry.dd: Opens the file as it was before this commit.
Opens the current version from your working copy.
Restores the file to its state in this commit.
Compares this commit's version with the previous one.
Compares this commit's version with your working copy.
When you select a range of commits, compares the two endpoint versions of the file.

section.p: When you select a range of commits, the bottom-left pane identifies the two revisions being compared (the newest and oldest in your selection) and the bottom-right pane lists the files that changed between them.

When you select the row, these two panes show your pending changes instead: the bottom-left pane lists the and the bottom-right pane lists the , both kept in sync with the view. Right-click a file to stage, unstage, or discard it (see ).
